--- Email Out ---
 Subject: Clarification on Lab Safety Procedures

 Hi Dr. Rivera,

 Could you clarify whether we’re required to wear safety goggles during the entire organic chemistry lab or only during active experiments?

 Thanks,
 Olivia

 --- Email In ---
 Subject: Re: Clarification on Lab Safety Procedures

 Hi Olivia,

 Safety goggles must be worn at all times in the lab. Please review the updated lab safety manual attached.

 Regards,
 Dr. Alejandro Rivera

 --- Attachment ---
 Organic Chemistry Lab Safety Guidelines 2025

 Department of Chemistry  
 University Laboratory Safety Manual  
 Updated: January 2025

 Table of Contents

 1. Introduction  
 2. General Conduct and Responsibilities  
 3. Personal Protective Equipment (PPE)  
 4. Laboratory Attire  
 5. Chemical Handling and Storage  
 6. Equipment Usage  
 7. Emergency Procedures  
 8. Waste Disposal  
 9. Housekeeping and Maintenance  
 10. Specific Hazards in Organic Chemistry Labs  
 11. Reporting Incidents and Near Misses  
 12. Training and Compliance  
 13. Acknowledgment of Guidelines

 ---

 1. Introduction

 The purpose of this document is to outline the safety procedures for all students, staff, and visitors working in the Organic Chemistry Laboratories at the University. Adherence to these guidelines is mandatory and essential for maintaining a safe environment, preventing accidents, and ensuring compliance with university policy and relevant legislation.

 - All laboratory users are expected to conduct themselves professionally.
 - Do not engage in horseplay, practical jokes, or any behavior that could compromise safety.
 - Always be aware of your surroundings and activities occurring in the lab.
 Personal Protective Equipment (PPE)

 a) Safety Goggles

 - Respirators are required only under special circumstances; consult your supervisor if unsure.
 - Closed-toe shoes are mandatory; sandals or open footwear are strictly prohibited.

 Proper attire is essential for minimizing exposure risks.

 - Long pants covering legs entirely are required.
 - Avoid loose clothing that could catch on equipment or become contaminated.
 - Long hair must be tied back securely above shoulder length.
 - All containers must be clearly labeled with chemical name, concentration (if applicable), hazard information, date received/prepared, and owner’s initials.

 - Segregate incompatible chemicals as per storage guidelines (acids away from bases, oxidizers from organics).
 - Flammable solvents must be stored in designated flammable cabinets.
 - Return chemicals to proper storage after use; do not leave containers open or unattended.

 - When Bunsen burners are necessary, ensure that flammable materials are cleared from the vicinity.

2. General Conduct and Responsibilities

 - Know the location of safety equipment (fire extinguishers, eyewash stations, safety showers, first aid kits).
 - Report unsafe conditions or equipment malfunctions immediately to the instructor or laboratory supervisor.

 3. Wearing appropriate PPE is mandatory at all times within the laboratory space.

 - ANSI-approved chemical splash goggles must be worn at all times upon entering the laboratory, regardless of whether active experimentation is occurring.
 - Prescription glasses alone do not provide adequate protection; over-goggles must be used if prescription lenses are required.
 - Face shields may be used in addition to goggles when there is risk of explosive reactions or large splashes, but never as a replacement for goggles.

 b) Gloves

 - Nitrile gloves are provided for general chemical handling; consult the glove compatibility chart for specific chemicals.
 - Gloves should be changed immediately if torn or contaminated.
 - Remove gloves before touching personal items (phones, pens), leaving the lab, or using communal equipment such as computers.

 c) Lab Coats

 - Lab coats must be worn at all times within the laboratory.
 - The coat should cover arms completely and be buttoned up during work.
 - Lab coats contaminated by hazardous chemicals should be removed immediately and replaced.

 d) Additional PPE

 4. Laboratory Attire

 - Jewelry such as rings, bracelets, necklaces, and dangling earrings should not be worn in the lab.

 5. Chemical Handling and Storage

 a) Labeling

 b) Safe Handling Practices

 - Always read Safety Data Sheets (SDS) before handling new chemicals.
 - Use fume hoods for volatile substances or those producing toxic vapors.
 - Never taste or directly smell chemicals; use wafting technique if instructed to assess odor.

 c) Storage

 6. Equipment Usage

 a) Glassware

 - Inspect glassware for cracks or chips before use; damaged items must not be used.
 - Clean glassware thoroughly after each experiment and return it to its designated area.

 b) Heating Apparatus

 - Use heating mantles or hot plates rather than open flames whenever possible.
 c) Fume Hoods

 - Work with hazardous chemicals inside fume hoods with sash lowered as much as possible while allowing safe manipulation.
 - Do not store equipment permanently inside fume hoods unless specifically permitted.

 d) Electrical Equipment

 - Ensure hands are dry before using electrical apparatus.
 - Report any frayed cords or malfunctioning devices immediately.

 7. Emergency Procedures

 a) Fire

 - In case of fire, alert others immediately and evacuate according to posted evacuation routes.
 - If trained, use a fire extinguisher only if safe to do so.

 b) Chemical Spills

 - Small spills: Alert others nearby, clean using appropriate spill kits following SDS instructions.
 - Large spills: Evacuate area and inform supervisor; do not attempt cleanup without guidance.

 c) Eye Exposure

 - Use eyewash station immediately for at least 15 minutes; remove contact lenses if possible during flushing.

 d) Skin Exposure

 - Flush affected area with water for at least 15 minutes; remove contaminated clothing promptly.

 e) Medical Emergencies

 - Call campus emergency services (number posted near phone); provide details of incident and location.

 f) Safety Showers/Eyewash Stations

 - Know locations prior to beginning work in any new lab space.

 8. Waste Disposal

 a) Chemical Waste

 - Segregate waste according to type: halogenated/non-halogenated solvents, acids/bases, heavy metals, etc.
 - Do not dispose of chemicals down sinks unless explicitly permitted by guidelines.
 - Use appropriately labeled waste containers; keep lids closed when not adding waste.

 b) Sharps/Broken Glassware

 - Dispose of broken glassware in designated “broken glass” boxes only—not regular trash bins.
 - Needles/syringes must go into approved sharps containers regardless of contamination status.

 c) Biological Waste (if applicable)

 - Dispose in autoclave bags or biohazard bins as directed by instructor/supervisor.

 9. Housekeeping and Maintenance

 a) Workspace Organization

 - Keep benches clear except for materials needed for current experiment.
 - Clean up spills promptly; leave workspace clean for next user at end of session.

 b) Regular Inspections

 - Participate in scheduled inspections by staff; address noted deficiencies promptly.

 c) Shared Spaces/Equipment

 - Return communal equipment to its proper location after use; report damage/malfunction immediately.

 10. Specific Hazards in Organic Chemistry Labs

 a) Flammable Liquids/Solvents

 - Common solvents (e.g. , diethyl ether, acetone, hexane) have low flash points—keep away from heat sources/open flames.
 - Store bulk quantities in flammable cabinets only; limit amounts kept on bench tops during experiments.

 b) Toxic Chemicals/Reagents

 - Some reagents (e.g. , cyanides, diazomethane) require special authorization/training—do not handle without supervision.
 - Use secondary containment when transporting toxic substances outside fume hood areas.

 c) Reactive Chemicals/Pyrophorics

 - Pyrophoric reagents ignite spontaneously on contact with air—use inert gas lines/glove boxes if required by protocol.
 - Review SDS and procedural guides before handling unfamiliar reactive chemicals.

 d) Compressed Gases/Cylinders

 - Secure cylinders upright with chains/straps at all times; cap cylinders when not in use.
 - Open valves slowly; never force connections or modify regulators without training.

 e) Glassware Under Pressure/Vacuum

 - Inspect vacuum lines/glassware regularly for cracks/stress points; shield setups where explosion risk exists.
 
 11. Reporting Incidents and Near Misses

 a) Incident Reporting Procedure

 1. Notify your instructor/supervisor immediately following any accident/injury/exposure/near miss—even if no injury occurred.
 2. Complete an incident report form within 24 hours (forms available from department office or online).
 3. Follow up with university health services if medical attention is needed.

 b) Confidentiality & No Retaliation Policy 

 Reporting incidents helps prevent future accidents—no disciplinary action will result from honest reporting unless gross negligence is involved.

 12. Training and Compliance 

 a) Mandatory Training Sessions 

 All users must complete:
 1. Initial laboratory safety orientation
 2. Annual refresher courses
 3. Specialized training for unique hazards/equipment (as determined by supervisor)

 b) Documentation 

 Sign-in sheets will verify attendance at training sessions; records maintained by department safety officer.

 c) Enforcement 

 Repeated violations of safety protocols may result in removal from laboratory privileges pending review by department chairperson.


 13. Acknowledgment of Guidelines 

 All students/staff/visitors must sign a copy of these guidelines prior to beginning work in the organic chemistry laboratory each semester.


 For questions about these guidelines or clarification on any procedure outlined herein, contact Dr. Alejandro Rivera at [department email address] or consult your assigned laboratory supervisor.


 Appendix: Quick Reference Checklist  

 Before Entering Lab:
 – Wear lab coat
 – Put on safety goggles
 – Secure long hair/tie back
 – Remove jewelry
 – Wear closed-toe shoes
 – Ensure pants cover legs fully  

 During Lab Work:
 – Keep goggles/lab coat on at all times
 – Use gloves when handling chemicals/glassware
 – Know location of safety equipment
 – Label all containers clearly
 – Work inside fume hood as needed  

 Before Leaving Lab:
 – Dispose waste properly
 – Clean workspace/glassware/equipment
 – Remove gloves/lab coat/goggles only after leaving lab area  

 Failure to comply with any part of these guidelines may result in disciplinary action according to university policy.

a) Flammable Liquids/Solvents

- Common solvents (e.g., diethyl ether, acetone, hexane) have low flash points—keep away from heat sources/open flames.
- Store bulk quantities in flammable cabinets only; limit amounts kept on bench tops during experiments.

b) Toxic Chemicals/Reagents

- Some reagents (e.g., cyanides, diazomethane) require special authorization/training—do not handle without supervision.
- Use secondary containment when transporting toxic substances outside fume hood areas.

--- Email Out ---
Subject: Clarification on Lab Safety Procedures

Hi Dr.
Rivera,

Could you clarify whether we’re required to wear safety goggles during the entire organic chemistry lab or only during active experiments?

Thanks,
Olivia

--- Email In ---
Subject: Re: Clarification on Lab Safety Procedures

Hi Olivia,

Safety goggles must be worn at all times in the lab.
Please review the updated lab safety manual attached.

Regards,
Dr.
Alejandro Rivera

--- Attachment ---
Organic Chemistry Lab Safety Guidelines 2025

Department of Chemistry  
University Laboratory Safety Manual  
Updated: January 2025

Table of Contents

Introduction  
General Conduct and Responsibilities  
Personal Protective Equipment (PPE)  
Laboratory Attire  
Chemical Handling and Storage  
Equipment Usage  
Emergency Procedures  
Waste Disposal  
Housekeeping and Maintenance  
Specific Hazards in Organic Chemistry Labs  
Reporting Incidents and Near Misses  
Training and Compliance  
Acknowledgment of Guidelines

---

Introduction

The purpose of this document is to outline the safety procedures for all students, staff, and visitors working in the Organic Chemistry Laboratories at the University.
Adherence to these guidelines is mandatory and essential for maintaining a safe environment, preventing accidents, and ensuring compliance with university policy and relevant legislation.

General Conduct and Responsibilities

- All laboratory users are expected to conduct themselves professionally.
- Do not engage in horseplay, practical jokes, or any behavior that could compromise safety.
- Always be aware of your surroundings and activities occurring in the lab.
- Know the location of safety equipment (fire extinguishers, eyewash stations, safety showers, first aid kits).
- Report unsafe conditions or equipment malfunctions immediately to the instructor or laboratory supervisor.

Personal Protective Equipment (PPE)

Wearing appropriate PPE is mandatory at all times within the laboratory space.

a) Safety Goggles

- ANSI-approved chemical splash goggles must be worn at all times upon entering the laboratory, regardless of whether active experimentation is occurring.
- Prescription glasses alone do not provide adequate protection; over-goggles must be used if prescription lenses are required.
- Face shields may be used in addition to goggles when there is risk of explosive reactions or large splashes, but never as a replacement for goggles.

b) Gloves

- Nitrile gloves are provided for general chemical handling; consult the glove compatibility chart for specific chemicals.
- Gloves should be changed immediately if torn or contaminated.
- Remove gloves before touching personal items (phones, pens), leaving the lab, or using communal equipment such as computers.

c) Lab Coats

- Lab coats must be worn at all times within the laboratory.
- The coat should cover arms completely and be buttoned up during work.
- Lab coats contaminated by hazardous chemicals should be removed immediately and replaced.

d) Additional PPE

- Respirators are required only under special circumstances; consult your supervisor if unsure.
- Closed-toe shoes are mandatory; sandals or open footwear are strictly prohibited.

Laboratory Attire

Proper attire is essential for minimizing exposure risks.

- Long pants covering legs entirely are required.
- Avoid loose clothing that could catch on equipment or become contaminated.
- Long hair must be tied back securely above shoulder length.
- Jewelry such as rings, bracelets, necklaces, and dangling earrings should not be worn in the lab.

Chemical Handling and Storage

a) Labeling

- All containers must be clearly labeled with chemical name, concentration (if applicable), hazard information, date received/prepared, and owner’s initials.

b) Safe Handling Practices

- Always read Safety Data Sheets (SDS) before handling new chemicals.
- Use fume hoods for volatile substances or those producing toxic vapors.
- Never taste or directly smell chemicals; use wafting technique if instructed to assess odor.

c) Storage

- Segregate incompatible chemicals as per storage guidelines (acids away from bases, oxidizers from organics).
- Flammable solvents must be stored in designated flammable cabinets.
- Return chemicals to proper storage after use; do not leave containers open or unattended.

Equipment Usage

a) Glassware

- Inspect glassware for cracks or chips before use; damaged items must not be used.
- Clean glassware thoroughly after each experiment and return it to its designated area.

b) Heating Apparatus

- Use heating mantles or hot plates rather than open flames whenever possible.
- When Bunsen burners are necessary, ensure that flammable materials are cleared from the vicinity.

c) Fume Hoods

- Work with hazardous chemicals inside fume hoods with sash lowered as much as possible while allowing safe manipulation.
- Do not store equipment permanently inside fume hoods unless specifically permitted.

d) Electrical Equipment

- Ensure hands are dry before using electrical apparatus.
- Report any frayed cords or malfunctioning devices immediately.

Emergency Procedures

a) Fire

- In case of fire, alert others immediately and evacuate according to posted evacuation routes.
- If trained, use a fire extinguisher only if safe to do so.

b) Chemical Spills

- Small spills: Alert others nearby, clean using appropriate spill kits following SDS instructions.
- Large spills: Evacuate area and inform supervisor; do not attempt cleanup without guidance.

c) Eye Exposure

- Use eyewash station immediately for at least 15 minutes; remove contact lenses if possible during flushing.

d) Skin Exposure

- Flush affected area with water for at least 15 minutes; remove contaminated clothing promptly.

e) Medical Emergencies

- Call campus emergency services (number posted near phone); provide details of incident and location.

f) Safety Showers/Eyewash Stations

- Know locations prior to beginning work in any new lab space.

Waste Disposal

a) Chemical Waste

- Segregate waste according to type: halogenated/non-halogenated solvents, acids/bases, heavy metals, etc.
- Do not dispose of chemicals down sinks unless explicitly permitted by guidelines.
- Use appropriately labeled waste containers; keep lids closed when not adding waste.

b) Sharps/Broken Glassware

- Dispose of broken glassware in designated “broken glass” boxes only—not regular trash bins.
- Needles/syringes must go into approved sharps containers regardless of contamination status.

c) Biological Waste (if applicable)

- Dispose in autoclave bags or biohazard bins as directed by instructor/supervisor.

Housekeeping and Maintenance

a) Workspace Organization

- Keep benches clear except for materials needed for current experiment.
- Clean up spills promptly; leave workspace clean for next user at end of session.

b) Regular Inspections

- Participate in scheduled inspections by staff; address noted deficiencies promptly.

c) Shared Spaces/Equipment

- Return communal equipment to its proper location after use; report damage/malfunction immediately.

Specific Hazards in Organic Chemistry Labs

a) Flammable Liquids/Solvents

- Common solvents (e.g.
, diethyl ether, acetone, hexane) have low flash points—keep away from heat sources/open flames.
- Store bulk quantities in flammable cabinets only; limit amounts kept on bench tops during experiments.

b) Toxic Chemicals/Reagents

- Some reagents (e.g.
, cyanides, diazomethane) require special authorization/training—do not handle without supervision.
- Use secondary containment when transporting toxic substances outside fume hood areas.

c) Reactive Chemicals/Pyrophorics

- Pyrophoric reagents ignite spontaneously on contact with air—use inert gas lines/glove boxes if required by protocol.
- Review SDS and procedural guides before handling unfamiliar reactive chemicals.

d) Compressed Gases/Cylinders

- Secure cylinders upright with chains/straps at all times; cap cylinders when not in use.
- Open valves slowly; never force connections or modify regulators without training.

e) Glassware Under Pressure/Vacuum

- Inspect vacuum lines/glassware regularly for cracks/stress points; shield setups where explosion risk exists.
 
Reporting Incidents and Near Misses

a) Incident Reporting Procedure

Notify your instructor/supervisor immediately following any accident/injury/exposure/near miss—even if no injury occurred.
Complete an incident report form within 24 hours (forms available from department office or online).
Follow up with university health services if medical attention is needed.

b) Confidentiality & No Retaliation Policy 

Reporting incidents helps prevent future accidents—no disciplinary action will result from honest reporting unless gross negligence is involved.

Training and Compliance 

a) Mandatory Training Sessions 

All users must complete:
Initial laboratory safety orientation
Annual refresher courses
Specialized training for unique hazards/equipment (as determined by supervisor)

b) Documentation 

Sign-in sheets will verify attendance at training sessions; records maintained by department safety officer.

c) Enforcement 

Repeated violations of safety protocols may result in removal from laboratory privileges pending review by department chairperson.


Acknowledgment of Guidelines 

All students/staff/visitors must sign a copy of these guidelines prior to beginning work in the organic chemistry laboratory each semester.


For questions about these guidelines or clarification on any procedure outlined herein, contact Dr.
Alejandro Rivera at [department email address] or consult your assigned laboratory supervisor.


Appendix: Quick Reference Checklist  

Before Entering Lab:
– Wear lab coat
– Put on safety goggles
– Secure long hair/tie back
– Remove jewelry
– Wear closed-toe shoes
– Ensure pants cover legs fully  

During Lab Work:
– Keep goggles/lab coat on at all times
– Use gloves when handling chemicals/glassware
– Know location of safety equipment
– Label all containers clearly
– Work inside fume hood as needed  

Before Leaving Lab:
– Dispose waste properly
– Clean workspace/glassware/equipment
– Remove gloves/lab coat/goggles only after leaving lab area  

Failure to comply with any part of these guidelines may result in disciplinary action according to university policy.
